title: Per-document history and diff: lore history/diff/show, keyed by OKF id not path
description: ODOC-231 Decision §1 (docs/adr/ground-lore-version-control-in-git-with-committed-citations-and-a-derived-index.md, opum-doc repo). Document identity is the OKF id, never the path, so rename becomes a metadata event; a moved doc leaves a moved_to: tombstone. Extraction is a single git log --raw -M pass over docs/ (rename detection is free in a full-history pass). --follow is prohibited (measurably wrong: 120 vs 140 commits on the same file in the ADR's own measurement, not merely slow). History simplification policy (--full-history --simplify-merges) must be stated in the command contract, not inherited by accident. Version identity is the blob SHA, not the commit. A revision has two content-addressed slots (frontmatter, body), each diffed by its own rules. Restore is forward-only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore history <id> lists (commit, timestamp, blob_sha) per version via git log --raw -M over docs/, keyed by OKF id and surviving renames via a moved_to: tombstone
lore diff <id> <a> <b> names two blob SHAs, with structural diff for the YAML frontmatter slot and text diff for the markdown body slot
lore show <id> --as-of <T> resolves the version current at time T
--follow is never used internally; the command contract states --full-history --simplify-merges explicitly
A restore creates a new current version; nothing rewrites history
